Tom — thanks for the clear asks. High level first — we support both topologies you described and price them differently:

- Separate per-region pools (active in each region): billed as two dedicated pools; each pool is sized/committed independently. Replication is not charged separately beyond the per-pool cost, but there is an incremental premium for cross-region synchronous KV/replication support if you require active-active consistency.
- Active-primary US + cold DR EU: billed as one active pool + a standby (reduced billing) DR pool; we typically offer 1–3 months of standby credits as part of committal discounts for multi-region failover.

Can I loop in Sean (commercial lead) for a pricing grid and Dev (infra) for a quick technical sizing note? If you can share estimated peak tokens/sec or concurrent requests per region that helps. I can follow up with a draft term sheet.

Tom / Grace — following up with a concrete commercial starting point. Summary below (ballpark, subject to final sizing):

Option A — Separate per-region pools (active-active)
- Commit: 20 dedicated GPU slots US + 10 dedicated GPU slots EU
- List rate: $X,XXX per GPU-slot/month (see attached capacity_breakdown.xlsx)
- Discount: 18% on committed capacity for 24-month term
- Notes: Active-active simplifies RTO/RPO but you pay for capacity in both regions.

Option B — Active-primary US + cold DR EU (standby)
- Commit: 30 dedicated GPU slots US primary + 5 standby slots EU
- Standby credit: first 60 days of standby billed at 0% (credit), then 50% of list for next 10 months unless activated
- Discount: 22% on committed US capacity for 18-month term
- Notes: Lower monthly bill; DR activation triggers billed ramp. Cross-region routing used for warm-latency probes incurs a small egress/replication fee (~Y% of bill).

Cross-region routing policy options we can include in contract:
1) Passive probing only (no user traffic): minimal replication fee, standby credits apply.
2) <5% steady-state traffic to DR (keeps caches warm): counts as metered usage against primary commit; additional small cross-region routing surcharge.
3) Active-active traffic split (50/50): effectively two full pools — price as Option A.

Attached: capacity_breakdown.xlsx (example mapping by GPU-type and expected throughput per model). I'll also drop a short term sheet (v3) with these options for you to review. If you give us expected 95th-percentile tokens/sec per region, we can convert to recommended slots.

Quick technical notes to help sizing decisions:

- Active-active: ideal if you need sub-500ms regional failover and are willing to pay for two hot pools. It keeps KV caches local per region and avoids bulk state transfer on failover.
- Active-primary + cold DR: cheaper but expect RTO in the 2–6 minute range unless you keep a small warm fraction of traffic hitting DR (we recommend maintaining ~2–3% warm traffic to keep KV warm; this reduces ramp time to under 60s).
- Cross-region routing surcharge: this largely covers increased network egress and cross-region KV replication bandwidth during warm probes. In practice, teams save more than the surcharge when standby credits are part of the commit.

If you want, we can propose a hybrid: keep 10% of capacity in the EU as a warm pool (billed at 30% of list) with automated ramp policy and health-based routing. That often hits the sweet spot for RTO vs cost.

Technical caveat: model quantization/sequence-length profiles matter — the spreadsheet assumes 8-bit quantized models and average seq len 64 tokens; if your workloads are longer, recommended slots increase.

- Dev
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Tom — good news, we can accommodate both asks for an 18-month pilot commit:

- Standby credit: we will add an extra 60 days (2 months) of standby credit in year 1 for the EU DR pool (in addition to the standard 60-day credit), effectively giving you ~120 days of zero-bill standby for DR in year 1.
- Cross-region surcharge cap: we'll include a cap equal to 8% of the monthly committed spend for the first 6 months; after that we'll transition to measured surcharges per contract (this cap is only applied when failover has not been invoked).

Commercial offer (summary):
- 18-month commit: 30 GPU slots US primary (quantized profile, avg seq 64) + 6 EU warm slots (billed at 30% for warm fraction until activated).
- Upfront discount: 20% on committed spend.
- DR standby credits: first 120 days zero-bill for EU standby; next 9 months billed at 50% until activation.
- DocuSign: https://docusign.com/ACME-RI-2027-01
- Attach: ACME_term_sheet_v3.pdf (term sheet with the standby credit language and surcharge cap)
